services.hero.title: Our Services & Expertise
services.hero.subtitle: From rigorous collection to exceptional processing, discover how ECAKOOG shapes a sustainable, value-creating cocoa supply chain.
services.card.collect.title: Purchasing, Collection & Packaging
services.card.collect.desc: Rigorous collection ensuring full traceability and optimal quality right from harvest.
services.card.export.desc: Access to international markets with certified products and added-value creation.
services.card.transform.desc: Artisanal processing of cocoa beans to create unique value.
svc.collect.h2: “Better collection to ensure the success of an agricultural season.”
svc.collect.p1: The heart of our business remains the collection of quality beans from our members, an activity that follows a rigorous and well-defined process. This process begins with identifying our producers and their plots, according to the criteria of the sustainability program they belong to. We train our producers in good environmental and agricultural practices, so that they ensure optimal sanitary and agronomic maintenance of their plots while complying with applicable standards. We also teach them the best practices for harvesting, pod-breaking, fermentation, drying and sorting of beans.
svc.collect.p2: The quality beans produced by our members are then collected in the section warehouses, then transported to the central warehouse, after passing the purchase control and being recorded in our traceability chain. We buy our producers' beans at the price set by the Coffee and Cocoa Council for the current season, and we subsequently pay them a premium, within the limit of the margin allocated to the sustainability program. Collection is an activity that requires a great deal of attention and precision, as it is essential to establish the complete traceability system of the supply chain within our cooperative. We ensure physical and digital traceability, which allows us to track the flow of cocoa beans and the financial flows between the cooperative and the producers.
svc.collect.p3: We have an efficient logistics service, made up of 38 collection vehicles, 5 trailers and 9 storage warehouses. This allows us to collect our members' beans across all our sections and branches. Thus, we collect more than 10,000,000 kg of beans from more than 10,500 producers, spread across 7 branches, 86 sections and more than 900 delegates.
svc.collect.services.title: Our Services
svc.collect.figures.title: Key Figures
svc.collect.figures.text: More than 10,000,000 kg of beans collected from 10,500 producers spread across 7 branches and 86 sections. A network of more than 900 delegates ensures constant connection with our members.
svc.export.h2: Export: far more than a commercial outlet, a driver of recognition and competitiveness.
svc.export.p1: In 2020, ECAKOOG established itself as a cocoa exporter, taking a decisive step in its development. This strategic choice reflects our determination not only to produce, but to directly add value to the work of our more than 10,000 producers. By engaging in international markets, we have turned our expertise into genuine added value, guaranteeing the quality, traceability and sustainability of every exported bean.
svc.export.p2: Export represents far more to us than a commercial outlet: it is a driver of recognition and competitiveness. It allows us to showcase Ivorian cocoa, strengthen the credibility of our cooperative and offer our partners a responsible and inclusive supply chain. With our fine flavor cocoa, we target niche markets so that the world can discover the unique flavors of our terroir, a symbol of excellence and innovation.
svc.export.impact.text: This approach brings real added value to the cocoa sector in Côte d'Ivoire, by addressing issues such as farmer poverty, the imbalance in profit distribution, deforestation, child labor, and discrimination against women.
svc.transform.h2: Artisanal processing of cocoa beans (roasted and shelled beans)
svc.transform.p1: The cooperative has initiated impactful projects for cocoa farmers while remaining firmly committed to excellence, sustainability and quality.
svc.transform.p2: "Fine flavour" cocoa is the cooperative's gem. It is obtained by following a quality process involving the selection of the right pods, then the treatment of the beans, from harvest through fermentation and drying to roasting and hand-shelling, by farmers' wives trained by Axel Emmanuel, the renowned Ivorian chocolatier with multiple international awards.
svc.transform.impact.text: By promoting local processing through artisanal initiatives, we not only add value to our exceptional cocoa but also contribute to the economic empowerment of our farmers' wives.
kog.hero.subtitle: Discover our program dedicated to socio-environmental sustainability, human development and the promotion of an exceptional specialty cocoa.
kog.intro.intrants: We encourage our farmers to adopt environmentally friendly practices by producing and using organic fertilizers and pesticides. This not only preserves the fertility of our soils and the health of our producers, but also guarantees high-quality cocoa, grown in symbiosis with nature.
kog.intro.finesaveur: Our exclusive terroir and our perfect mastery of post-harvest processes (delicate fermentation and drying) allow us to produce an exceptional "fine flavor" cocoa. Its unique aromatic notes are highly prized by artisan chocolatiers worldwide seeking a complex and authentic flavor profile.
kog.intro.bancarisation: Financial empowerment goes hand in hand with security. We facilitate the opening of bank accounts (banking inclusion) for our producers, securing their monetary income. In addition, integrated health insurance coverage protects the health of farming families, ensuring peace of mind and income stability for the household year after year.
kog.intro.genre: Equal opportunity is at the heart of our cooperative model. We carry out decisive actions for the empowerment of women in rural areas and implement strict monitoring and remediation programs to eradicate all the worst forms of child labor in our production areas.
kog.intro.agroforesterie: To effectively combat deforestation and climate change, we support our members in their transition to agroforestry. By carefully combining fruit and forest trees with our cocoa trees, we create a resilient, shaded and fertile ecosystem, ensuring diversified income for producers.
kog.agro.h2: Restoring landscapes, diversifying crops and protecting biodiversity
kog.agro.p1: Cocoa orchards have aged. To avoid the systematic resort to new forest areas and the increased use of chemical inputs, we must act. These practices threaten the environment and biodiversity, and concern our chocolatier partners.
kog.agro.p2: To reduce these impacts, ECAKOOG offers its farmers a new, better-suited approach: agroforestry. This method makes it possible to practice agriculture that respects the available land and biodiversity.
kog.agro.p3: This approach fosters the development of a new generation of farmers, contributes to the fight against global warming and allows producers to diversify their income thanks to the associated fruit and forest trees.
kog.agro.testimonial: "By fighting deforestation in our cocoa supply chain, we aim to further reduce our carbon footprint and support cocoa producers in developing farms that are better adapted to climate change. We already participate in the Koognagnan cocoa program and we plan to create community forests around our villages."
kog.banc.h2: Financial inclusion to modernize transactions and secure producers' income
kog.banc.p1: The cocoa value chain is well structured. However, our member producers do not have access to the services of banks, microfinance institutions and other formal financial institutions. The challenge is therefore to offer our members access to financial services that are both affordable and suited to our needs as farmers.
kog.banc.p2: Developing the financial system and improving financial inclusion are priorities for our cooperative enterprise. ECAKOOG, in collaboration with partner microfinance institutions, has raised producers' awareness of the importance of accessing formal financial services. This important effort has enabled more than 1,500 producers to be enrolled with active accounts.
kog.banc.p3: With a simple system, when producers are paid after their beans are weighed, they can decide how much they wish to receive in their bank account and how much they wish to receive in cash.
kog.banc.p4: The goal with the Koognagnan cocoa program is to provide bank accounts to 100% of our producers by 2027, to train them in sound financial education and to turn each of our members into agricultural entrepreneurs.
kog.banc.testimonial: "Banking inclusion transforms the lives of our producers. It gives them access to formal financial services, which offer them more security and opportunities. With their account, producers make wiser choices. They don't spend all their money on a whim, but manage it wisely."
kog.fine.h2: The fine flavor cocoa process: a value strategy based on taste
kog.fine.sub1: Our Fine Flavors: the excellence of Ivorian cocoa
kog.fine.p1: Each of our cocoa beans carries a story, a terroir and a unique identity. This is why we chose to showcase our fine flavor cocoas, born from expertise and rigorous selection among our producers. These precious beans stand out for their subtle aromas, their floral or fruity notes, and their gustatory richness that reflects the diversity of Ivorian terroirs.
kog.fine.p2: By embarking on the development of this exceptional cocoa, we target niche markets and high-end chocolate lovers around the world. Our ambition is to introduce the international consumer to the singularity of our flavors, while adding value to the work of our producers. With ECAKOOG, tasting cocoa means living an authentic sensory experience, where quality, traceability and sustainability combine to offer a unique product with real added value.
kog.fine.share.title: Value Sharing
kog.fine.share.intro: Our value-sharing strategy uses several mechanisms:
kog.fine.share.prime: Quality premium: Reward for superior-quality wet beans.
kog.fine.share.engagement: Full purchase commitment: Purchase of all certified beans, guaranteeing the producer's income.
kog.fine.share.bonus: Direct sale bonus: A specific amount charged to the client is paid back (30% in cash to producers, 70% for community projects).
kog.fine.engagements.title: Our Commitments
kog.fine.impact.title: Community Impact
kog.fine.impact.text: Thanks to the direct sale bonus, we fund essential community projects while directly increasing producers' income in cash.
kog.intrants.h2: Providing organic fertilizers and biopesticides for environmentally friendly production
kog.intrants.p1: To support the production of certified cocoa beans and master the entire supply chain, the Koognagnan Agricultural Cooperative Enterprise of Grogouya has taken steps to provide its producers with organic inputs in order to improve soil fertility, orchard treatment and the quality of harvested beans, thereby obtaining a more rewarding price thanks to market outlets.
kog.intrants.p2: ECAKOOG, supported by the Équité 2 program and other initiatives, has been able to put in place a set of measures.
kog.intrants.actions.title: Our Key Actions
kog.intrants.li2: Production and sale of organic inputs at lower cost
kog.intrants.testimonial: "My farm has completely changed. It has been regenerated thanks to good agricultural and environmental practices. Yields have increased, and I get better prices. This has helped us a lot. Thanks to Ecakoog, I have found my life again."
page.title.genre: Gender Promotion & Fight Against Child Labor - ECAKOOG
kog.genre.h1: Gender Promotion & Fight Against Child Labor
kog.genre.h2: Empowering women and fighting child labor: inclusive programs to strengthen equity
kog.genre.p1: In farming communities, and especially in the cocoa production chain, women are essential to the sustainability of the industry. Although cocoa is perceived as a male crop, women carry out nearly half of the work in the fields. Strengthening the social position and rights of women is the key to solving many challenges, including child labor.
kog.genre.p2: ECAKOOG is committed to producing sustainable cocoa beans with the inclusion of women and young people and without child labor or forced labor. Thanks to the "Gender Promotion" committee, several programs promote:
kog.genre.prog1: Women's acquisition of secured plots of land.
kog.genre.prog3: The creation of Village Savings and Credit Associations (VSLA).
kog.genre.p3: ECAKOOG has made gender promotion an essential pillar of its governance and its Koognagnan Cacao sustainability program.
kog.genre.results.title: Our Results
kog.genre.testimonial: "What gives me satisfaction is knowing that education and the inclusion of women are at the heart of our priorities. Empowering women is the most effective way to fight child labor. It is a mission we cherish every day at ECAKOOG."

rea.water.h1: Construction of water towers for five sections of the cooperative
rea.water.p1: Access to drinking water is a major challenge in the rural areas of Côte d'Ivoire. For ECAKOOG, the well-being of our producers and their families depends first and foremost on solid basic infrastructure.
rea.water.p2: With this in mind, we undertook the construction and commissioning of water towers in five of our strategic sections. This ambitious project aims to sustainably transform the daily lives of rural communities by providing them with a clean, reliable and lasting source of water.
rea.water.p3: By facilitating access to water, we not only help improve hygiene and public health, but we also free up precious time for women and children, who are often tasked with fetching water. This project is fully in line with our vision of an agriculture that develops people as much as it produces value.
rea.water.figures.title: Key Project Figures
page.title.rea.kits: Education: School Kits for All - ECAKOOG
rea.kits.h1: Distribution of supplies and school kits for members' children
rea.kits.p1: Education is the key to a better future. For ECAKOOG, supporting the schooling of our producers' children is an absolute priority and a powerful lever in the fight against child labor.
rea.kits.p2: Every year, as the school year approaches, the cooperative organizes a large campaign to distribute complete school kits (bags, notebooks, pens, geometry tools, etc.). This initiative aims to ease the financial burden on families and ensure that every child has the tools needed to succeed in their studies.
rea.kits.p3: By investing in education, we build the foundations of a prosperous community aware of the importance of knowledge. This is our contribution so that the future generations of Grogouya and our areas of operation can flourish and uphold the values of our cooperative.
rea.kits.obj.title: Goals of the Initiative
rea.kits.li1: Reduce the dropout rate in our areas of operation.
rea.kits.li2: Effectively fight child labor by promoting access to school.
rea.kits.li3: Ease the budget of farming households at the start of the school year.
rea.school.h1: Construction of a three-classroom primary school in Grogouya
rea.school.p1: The proximity of a school is a decisive factor for the effective schooling of children in rural areas. In 2019, ECAKOOG took a major step in its social commitment by funding the construction of a complete school building.
rea.school.p2: Located at the heart of our area of operation, this school includes three modern classrooms, a head teacher's office and latrines. This infrastructure meets a pressing need of local populations, who were previously forced to travel long distances to send their children to school.
rea.school.p3: This project, entirely funded by our members' certification premiums, shows that the cooperative model is a driver of concrete change. By providing a decent and safe study environment, we sow the seeds of success for the future generations of Grogouya.

actu.rabo.pagetitle: Rabo Rural Fund visits ECAKOOG - ECAKOOG
actu.rabo.p1: On January 23, 2026, we had the great pleasure of welcoming the teams of Rabo Rural Fund, one of our financial partners.
actu.rabo.p2: This visit was a moment of friendly and constructive exchanges about our future collaboration opportunities.
actu.rabo.p3: We warmly thank the Rabo Rural Fund team for their presence and their commitment:
actu.rabo.li1: Peter Veening, Africa Program Manager - Rabo Rural Fund
actu.rabo.li2: Arnaud Tchogna, Impact Finance Consultant - Côte d'Ivoire
actu.rabo.li3: Blaise Gouan, Consultant, specialist in professional agricultural organization
actu.rabo.p4: These moments of sharing strengthen the will to work together and confirm a common ambition: to support producers, structure the cocoa sector and generate a lasting, positive impact.
actu.cemoi.pagetitle: ECAKOOG at CEMOI's 10th anniversary celebration - ECAKOOG
actu.cemoi.h1: ECAKOOG at the 10th anniversary celebration of the CEMOI Côte d'Ivoire chocolate factory
actu.cemoi.p1: On February 5 and 6, 2026, the Cemoi Chocolate Factory celebrated its 10th anniversary. A highlight that brought together 41 cooperatives and players from the cocoa value chain.
actu.cemoi.p2: ECAKOOG, through the presence of Ginette Kouamé, Director, and Ousmane TRAORE, Chairman of the Board of Directors, had the honor of taking part as a CEMOI partner cooperative and beneficiary of the Cocoa Transparency program.
actu.cemoi.p3: This celebration was an opportunity to retrace the chocolate factory's journey and highlight the path travelled.
actu.cemoi.p4: The program featured an official ceremony and a guided tour of the industrial site and chocolate factory, offering an immersion into CEMOI's know-how.
actu.cemoi.p5: On the occasion of this anniversary, a Cocoa Transparency seminar was also held on February 5, with insights into the Cocoa Transparency program and discussions on traceability and developments in the cocoa market.
actu.cemoi.p6: Beyond the discussions, these encounters were above all human, rich and inspiring.
actu.cemoi.p7: Many thanks for this invitation and these moments of sharing, and happy anniversary to the CEMOI Côte d'Ivoire chocolate factory!
actu.salon.pagetitle: ECAKOOG at the Chocolate and Pastry Show in Paris - ECAKOOG
actu.salon.p1: From October 28 to November 2, 2025, ECAKOOG took part in the Chocolate and Pastry Show in Paris, a major international event for the world of cocoa.
actu.salon.p2: This participation was led by the Director, Ginette Kouame, and the Chairman, Ousmane TRAORE, proud to represent ECAKOOG's producers on the international stage.
actu.salon.p3: This participation was made possible thanks to the support of AVSF (Agronomes et Vétérinaires Sans Frontières).
actu.salon.p4: We were happy to present our processed products for the first time:
actu.salon.p5: The public's reception was warm and enthusiastic, confirming that local processing represents real added value.
par.subtitle: COLLABORATION
par.title: Our collective strength
par.desc: To consolidate our activities and support our hardworking producers, ECAKOOG collaborates with several major organizations and institutions. These partnerships allow us to ensure the sustainability of our business and the well-being of our members.
ap.pca.p1: For several years, Côte d'Ivoire has been the world leader in cocoa bean production. This performance is the fruit of the hard work of our brave parent farmers. However, they do not always fully enjoy the rewards of their efforts.
ap.pca.p2: To address this, we young executives, sons and daughters of producers, decided to come together to create a cooperative named ECAKOOG COOP-CA (Koognagnan Agricultural Cooperative Enterprise of Grogouya), with the mission of contributing to improving the living and working conditions of our parent farmers by offering them a better framework to market their products. Our goal is to build a modern, sustainable and environmentally friendly agriculture.
ap.pca.signature: Chairman of the Board of Directors
ap.who.intro1: ECAKOOG is a cocoa bean exporting cooperative, respectful of its partners' requirements and of European standards, and a guarantor of the quality of its producers' beans. Today, it has exactly 10,533 producers and 86 sections spread between the Lakota head office and seven (07) branches.
ap.who.intro2: With a production capacity estimated at 20,000 tonnes over an area of 22,076.81 ha, ECAKOOG promotes organic production by providing its members with natural and effective inputs, such as organic fertilizers and biopesticides. It also encourages crop diversification by integrating fruit trees, medicinal plants and forest species into its cocoa plots, in order to improve soil fertility, biodiversity and producers' income.
ap.who.objective.title: OUR OBJECTIVE
ap.who.objective.text: To collect, package, market, export and process our members' product into different flavors while contributing to improving cocoa farmers' income and promoting an agroecological approach in organic cocoa production.
ap.who.pillars.intro: ECAKOOG has its own sustainability program based on 5 essential pillars:
ap.pillar2: Production of organic cocoa and organic inputs
ap.pillar3: Banking inclusion and digitalization of financial transactions
ap.pillar4: Agroforestry and environmental preservation through landscape restoration
ap.pillar5: Gender promotion and the fight against child labor
ap.org.p1: ECAKOOG is made up of 4 statutory bodies: a General Assembly, a Board of Directors of 9 members, a Supervisory Board of 3 members and a Statutory Auditor. The cooperative is led by a Director and oversees an accounting, export, logistics and sustainability department, for a total of 85 employees.
ap.org.p2: Our governance reflects our commitment to transparency and efficiency. The General Assembly is the supreme decision-making body. It defines the cooperative's general policy.
ap.org.p3: The Board of Directors, made up of elected members, ensures the implementation of the General Assembly's decisions. The Executive Management handles day-to-day operational management.
ap.org.p4: To stay as close as possible to our producers, we have decentralized our activities across our 5 branches, thereby ensuring technical monitoring and efficient supply.
ap.stats.subtitle: IMPACT
ap.history.subtitle: OUR HISTORY
ap.history.subtitle2: From founding to export, the major milestones of our development.
ap.tl1.title: February - July 2012: Birth
ap.tl1.text: After awareness campaigns began in February and a register of 521 producers was set up, ECAKOOG was officially founded on July 14, 2012 in Grogouya (Lakota) with a capital of 10,420,000 F CFA.
ap.tl2.title: 2012 - 2014: Structuring
ap.tl2.text: Obtaining approval in October 2012 marked our beginnings. In August 2013, we became a cooperative society, followed by our registration with the RSC in January 2014.
ap.tl3.title: October 2015: Recognition
ap.tl3.text: Record volume of 5,000 tonnes reached. We were awarded best cooperative of the Divo regional delegation (JNCC) and obtained UTZ certification for our good practices.
ap.tl4.title: 2017 - 2019: Diversification
ap.tl4.text: Obtained the Fairtrade label in 2017. Launched fine flavor cocoa production in 2019, the year we officially became ECAKOOG COOP-CA.
ap.tl5.title: 2020 - 2021: Export & Organic
ap.tl5.text: Development of the internal sustainability program Koognanan cacao. We became an exporting company in October 2020 and obtained Organic certification in May 2021.
ap.tl6.title: 2022 - 2024: National Expansion
ap.tl6.text: Creation of 5 branches in 2022, followed by 2 additional ones (San-Pedro and Duékoué) in May 2024, bringing us ever closer to our producers.
